status: Design budgets; not full PVT/local-mismatch qualification
basis: Rounded design budgets informed by the historical V2.0.3 SS/SF envelope and V2.1.0 waveform screening. The initial 1200 ps budget missed the SS 16x16 sequence read deadline, so the smallest budget is 1600 ps. Historical fits are not executed at runtime. See docs/design/TIMING_LOOKUP_V2_1_0.md for exact coverage and limits. The initial 512-row budget missed SS distributed read (3.341 ns clock-to-data), so the 512-row budget is 3600 ps. V2.1.3 adds a separate budget for 10T cells: the V2.1.2 follow-up (docs/design/TIMING_FOLLOWUP_V2_1_2.md) found the shared 1600 ps class failing 16x16 10T with a column mux nominally and 8x4 under mismatch at SS 0.9 V / 125 C, and the V2.1.3 evidence run found the 16x16 10T sequence without a mux failing the same read-output checks; the 10T read port and the mux pass gate cost about 170 ps and 140 ps of the access window. The first evidence pass at a flat 200 ps above the shared classes failed the 128x8 10T mux read at 5.5 ns (output 40 ps before the deadline) and left only 125 ps at the 32x16 bound at 4.5 ns, so the 10T row budget grows with height and keeps at least 250 ps at every class bound; the 512-row class additionally needs the 10T read-disturb bump on the storage node to decay within the 0.1 VDD tolerance, which failed at 11 ns. See docs/design/TIMING_10T_BUDGET_V2_1_3.md for the evidence run.
policy: T = ceil_to_50ps(2 * max(row.half_period_ps, column.half_period_ps) * (1 + margin)); default margin 0.25. Round dimensions up to anchors, extrapolate the final geometric ladder beyond them and flag the result. The shared classes apply to every architecture without a variant entry; a variant keyed by cell_type (and mux, when given) replaces both ladders for that architecture and may never fall below the shared budget. Physical wiring still shares the classes; custom RC still requires waveform checks.

variants.basis: Row classes 2000/2200/2400/3200/5600 ps and column classes 200 ps above the shared ladder, with or without a column mux. The 10T read port discharges the replica bitline about 1 ps per row slower than 6T and its sense path adds a near-constant 200 ps, so the row budget grows with height. Rule: at least 250 ps between the local read output and the 1.2 T deadline at the class bound, nominal SS 0.9 V / 125 C (the 4.5 ns class left 125 ps at 32x16 and failed one mismatch seed). The 512-row class is set by the storage node, not the output: the 10T read-disturb bump (0.196 V against 0.131 V for 6T) decays with the bitline, which a 512-row array discharges slowly, so at 11 ns Q was still 0.108 V at the deadline against the 0.1 VDD tolerance; 14 ns gives the bitline about 5.6 ns. 5 ns up to 32 rows / 16 columns, 5.5 ns to 64 rows, 6 ns to 128, 8 ns to 256, 14 ns to 512.
